texts.preamble: Shiv Prasad vs State Of U.P. on 20 November, 2023 Author: Samit Gopal Bench: Samit Gopal High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad ? Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc:219602 Court No. - 69 Case :- Criminal Revision No. - 4067 of 2011 Revisionist :- Shiv Prasad Opposite Party :- State of U.P. Counsel for Revisionist :- Sharad Kumar Srivastava Counsel for Opposite Party :- Govt. Advocate Hon'ble Samit Gopal,J. 1. List revised.
texts.facts: The same are tagged with the present revision. The facts of the case are that the revisionist is a betel shop owner. The food analyst visited his shop on 07.09.2001 situated in Village Bahrampur, Police Station Thariyao, District Fatehpur where he found the revisionist to have displayed oil, spices, namkin, supari, desi katha and desi gutka for sale. He introduced himself to him and asked for a license for sale which was shown to him. On a suspicion of adulteration, he prepared form 6 and proceeded to take the sample of desi gutka for analysis but the accused refused to give him the said product. He further refused to sign on form 6 and even return it back. In the mean time, many persons as supporters of the revisionist came there who threatened him of not taking any sample. He prepared an inspection report of spot on which also the revisionist refused to sign even the public witnesses present there refused to sign. The inspection report and the sanction for prosecution obtained from C.M.O. concerned have been annexed with the complaint and a complaint has been filed against the revisionist. 6. In the statement recorded under section 251 Cr.P.C. of the accused/revisionist he stated of false implication and further stated that there was a demand of money by the complainant which was refused and as such due to the said enmity the present complaint has been filed. No defence evidence was led. In the trial, the Food Inspector H.S. Gupta was examined as P.W.-1. The present revision is thus before this Court assailing the said judgment and orders.
texts.arguments: 7. Learned counsel for the revisionist argued that the revisionist has been falsely implicated in the present case. It is argued that the admitted case of the prosecution is of no material being collected for analysis on a suspicion of it being adulterated. It is argued that except for the Food Inspector who was examined as P.W.-1 there is no other witness produced and examined before the trial court. It is argued that there is no independent person to support the prosecution story. Learned counsel for the revisionist has argued that the accused while giving an explanation under section 251 Cr.P.C. has stated a false implication due to ulterior motive as there was some illegal demand from him by the Food Inspector/complainant. It is argued that there is no credible evidence against him. The present revision be thus allowed. 8. Per contra, learned counsel for the State has opposed the prayer and arguments in the present revision and argued that the trial court has after considering the matter on its merit passed the Shiv Prasad vs State Of U.P. on 20 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183263650/ 2 impugned judgment and order without any irregularity or illegality. It is argued that the said judgment and order of the trial court has even been affirmed by the appellate court. It is argued that there is no irregularity and illegality and as such the revision be dismissed.
